# REST API for builders

This page lists the calls a builder needs. The workflow JSON itself is described in [workflow-format.md](workflow-format.md) and [tools-and-code.md](tools-and-code.md).

Personas, simulations and calls are documented in full at https://docs.freyavoice.ai. Workflow creation and the workflow JSON are not documented there. Use these pages for them.

Every call on this page is taken from a client that was run against the platform, unless a line says "not confirmed".

## Basics

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Base URL | `https://staging-app.freyavoice.ai` |
| Auth header | `Authorization: Bearer <your API key>`. Keys start with `fak_` |
| Content type | `Content-Type: application/json` |
| User-Agent | Required, and it must look like a browser. Example: `Mozilla/5.0 (my-builder)` |

A request without a browser-like `User-Agent` is rejected before it reaches the API. The response is an HTML page with `error code: 1010`. Many HTTP libraries send a default agent that is rejected, so set the header yourself.

The curl examples use these variables:

```bash
export FREYA_API_URL=https://staging-app.freyavoice.ai
export FREYA_API_KEY=fak_your_key
export UA="Mozilla/5.0 (my-builder)"
```

### Response envelope

Every JSON response has this shape:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": {
    "message": "text",
    "result": {}
  }
}
```

The payload is `data.result`. The field paths below are relative to `data.result`.

The reference client reads the wrapper keys named below (`workflow`, `simulation`, `iterations`, `workspaces`) and falls back to the bare payload if a key is missing. Do the same in your client.

An HTML response with status 404 means the route is wrong. Note that the workflow and call routes are singular (`/api/v2/workflow`, `/api/v2/call`) and the persona and simulation routes are plural.

## Workflows

### Create a workflow

`POST /api/v2/workflow`

The body holds a name and the workflow definition. The platform creates the agent together with the workflow.

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/workflow" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA" \
  -d '{"name": "my agent", "workflow": {"initial_node": "start", "nodes": {}, "global_nodes": {}}}'
```

| Path in `result` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `workflow.id` | The workflow id |
| `workflow.agentId` | The id of the agent that was created with it. Pass this as `agentId` to a simulation |

Put a complete workflow in `workflow`. The empty `nodes` object above only keeps the example short.

### Validate without saving (dry run)

`POST /api/v2/workflow?dryRun=true`

Same body as create. The platform runs its write validation and stores nothing.

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/workflow?dryRun=true" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA" \
  -d @request.json
```

The fields of the dry-run result are not documented. The reference client treats any HTTP error status as a failure and prints the response body.

Validation checks the schema. It also removes fields that do not belong to a node type without reporting them. For example `pre_actions` on a `conversation` node is dropped. Read a created workflow back if you are unsure what was stored.

### Update a workflow

`PUT /api/v2/workflow/{workflowId}`

```bash
curl -s -X PUT "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/workflow/$WORKFLOW_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA" \
  -d '{"workflow": {"initial_node": "start", "nodes": {}, "global_nodes": {}}}'
```

The body replaces the whole definition. A top-level key that your new definition leaves out is deleted, including `test_variables` and an `agent_config` that the platform filled in. Send the complete definition every time.

An update saves a new version and does NOT publish it. Simulations and calls run the published version, so after an update alone you are still testing the old phone agent. Publish the new version:

```bash
# newest version first
curl -s "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/versions/workflow/$WORKFLOW_ID?workspaceId=$WORKSPACE_ID" -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" -H "User-Agent: $UA"
# result.versions[] has id, versionNumber, isPublished

curl -s -X POST "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/versions/workflow/$WORKFLOW_ID/publish" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "User-Agent: $UA" \
  -d '{"versionId": "<id of the newest version>"}'
```

`freya.update_workflow` and `freya.save_workflow` do both steps. A run of a simulation reports the version it used as `agentVersionNumber`. Check it when a change seems to have no effect.

### Get a workflow

`GET /api/v2/workflow/{workflowId}`

```bash
curl -s "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/workflow/$WORKFLOW_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA"
```

The path is the same as for update. The reference client does not call this route, so the fields of its result are not confirmed.

## Workspace

`GET /api/v2/workspaces` lists the workspaces your key can see. The list is at `result.workspaces`. Each entry has an `id`.

```bash
curl -s "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/workspaces" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA"
```

List routes need the workspace id as a query parameter. The name of that parameter is not confirmed here. See https://docs.freyavoice.ai.

## Personas

A persona plays the caller in a simulation. It has a prompt and success criteria.

### Create personas

`POST /api/v2/personas`

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/personas" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA" \
  -d '{"personas": [{"name": "Late parcel", "prompt": "You are Dana Reed. Your parcel is five days late. Answer what you are asked in one short sentence.", "successCriteria": "The agent states the new delivery day.", "tags": ["practice"]}]}'
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `personas[].name` | Persona name |
| `personas[].prompt` | Instructions for the model that plays the caller |
| `personas[].successCriteria` | Text that the judge model checks after the call |
| `personas[].tags` | Array of strings |

The created personas are at `result.personas`, in request order. Each has an `id`.

### List personas

`GET /api/v2/personas`

```bash
curl -s "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/personas" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA"
```

Not confirmed: the reference client only creates personas. The path above is the create route with `GET`. This is a list route, so it needs the workspace query parameter mentioned above. Take the parameters and result fields from https://docs.freyavoice.ai.

## Simulations

A simulation runs your agent against personas. In `chat` mode the conversation is text only.

### Create a simulation

`POST /api/v2/simulations`

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/simulations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA" \
  -d '{
    "agentId": "AGENT_ID",
    "name": "practice run 1",
    "mode": "chat",
    "selectedPersonaIds": ["PERSONA_ID"],
    "customerVariablesMap": {"PERSONA_ID": {"customer_id": "c_123", "first_name": "Dana"}},
    "maxConcurrentCalls": 5,
    "runsPerPersona": 1,
    "maxCallDurationSeconds": 420,
    "assistantLlmOverride": {"provider": "experimental-5", "model": "experimental-5"},
    "routingLlmOverride": {"provider": "experimental-5", "model": "experimental-5"},
    "extractionLlmOverride": {"provider": "experimental-5", "model": "experimental-5"},
    "personaLlmOverride": {"provider": "google", "model": "gemini-3-flash-preview"},
    "analysisLlmOverride": {"provider": "google", "model": "gemini-3-flash-preview"}
  }'
```

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `agentId` | `workflow.agentId` from the create call |
| `name` | Name of the simulation |
| `mode` | `"chat"` for a text simulation |
| `selectedPersonaIds` | Persona ids to run |
| `customerVariablesMap` | Object keyed by persona id. Each value is the object of call variables for that persona's call |
| `maxConcurrentCalls` | How many calls run at the same time |
| `runsPerPersona` | Calls per persona |
| `maxCallDurationSeconds` | Limit for one call |
| `assistantLlmOverride` | Model for the dialogue call. Object with `provider` and `model` |
| `routingLlmOverride` | Model for the routing call |
| `extractionLlmOverride` | Model for the extraction call |
| `personaLlmOverride` | Model that plays the caller |
| `analysisLlmOverride` | Model that judges the success criteria |

Pass all three agent overrides (`assistantLlmOverride`, `routingLlmOverride`, `extractionLlmOverride`) on every simulation. An override you leave out falls back to the agent's default model. The values above are the ones the reference client uses. Use the models your event rules name.

The simulation id is at `result.simulation.id`.

### Poll a simulation

`GET /api/v2/simulations/{simulationId}`

```bash
curl -s "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/simulations/$SIM_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA"
```

Read `result.simulation.status`. Poll every 10 seconds until it is `completed`, `failed` or `paused`. Other status values are not listed in the sources.

### Talk to your workflow turn by turn

`POST /api/v2/chat/message` runs one turn against the published workflow, with no simulation and no queue. It answers in seconds, so it is the fastest way to see whether a workflow starts at all and what it says first.

```bash
curl -s -X POST "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/chat/message" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "User-Agent: $UA" \
  -d '{"workflowId": "'$WORKFLOW_ID'", "message": "Hello?", "customerVariables": {"customer_id": "c_test", "first_name": "Daniel", "last_name": "Reyes", "title": "Mr", "now": "2026-10-14T11:00"}}'
```

`result` has `response` (what the phone agent said) and `callId`. Send the next turn with the same `callId`. End it with `POST /api/v2/chat/end` and `{"callId": "..."}`.

Seen in tests, not guaranteed: a long turn can return 504, and when the first step is a code step the chat route may skip it, so values that step computes are empty. A bare 500 here means the workflow cannot start a call at all.

### List iterations

`GET /api/v2/simulations/{simulationId}/iterations`

```bash
curl -s "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/simulations/$SIM_ID/iterations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA"
```

An iteration is one execution of the simulation. The list is at `result.iterations`. The reference client takes the first entry's `id` right after a simulation finishes.

### Get an iteration's runs

`GET /api/v2/simulations/{simulationId}/iterations/{iterationId}`

```bash
curl -s "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/simulations/$SIM_ID/iterations/$ITERATION_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA"
```

`result` has `iteration`, `runs` and `runsTotal`. A run is one call with one persona.

| Field of a run | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `id` | Run id |
| `callId` | Id of the call. Use it to fetch the transcript |
| `personaId`, `personaName` | The persona that played the caller |
| `outcome` | Result of the success criteria, for example `fail` |
| `reason` | The judge's explanation |
| `turnCount` | Number of turns |
| `startedAt`, `endedAt` | Timestamps |

The route returns 30 runs unless you ask for more. Pass `limit` (100 at most) and `offset`, and read until a page comes back short. Compare the number you read with `runsTotal`. `freya.get_iteration` does this for you.

While a simulation is running, `outcome` is `queued` or `running` for the runs that have not finished.

## Calls

### Get a call with its transcript

`GET /api/v2/call/{callId}`

```bash
curl -s "$FREYA_API_URL/api/v2/call/$CALL_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $FREYA_API_KEY" \
  -H "User-Agent: $UA"
```

The call is at `result.call`.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `messages` | The event list of the call. See below |
| `transcript` | The conversation as one text string |
| `endedReason` | Why the call ended. For an `end_call` node it is the terminal's `function.name` |
| `duration` | Seconds |
| `successCriteriaResult` | Object with `success` and `reason` |

Each entry of `messages` has `role`, `message`, `nodeId`, `messageId` and `secondsFromStart`.

| `role` | `message` contains |
|---|---|
| `assistant` | What the agent said |
| `user` | What the caller said |
| `system` | A JSON string that describes one engine event |

System events seen in a trial call:

| `event` | Content |
|---|---|
| `node_enter` | `node`, `from_node`, `reason` |
| `function_call_start` | `function` and `args`. For an `api_call` the args are the full request: `url`, `method`, `headers`, `body` |
| `function_call_complete` | `function` and `result` |
| `route_evaluated` | `matched`, `from_node`, `target`, `reason`, a `branches` list with the result of every condition, and `variable_table` with all variables at that moment |
| `error` | `message` and `details` |

`route_evaluated` is the fastest way to learn why a transition did or did not fire. Each branch shows the variable, the operand and the result.

User and assistant messages in the trial call also carried a `workflowSnapshot` with `currentNode`, `previousNode`, `nodeTurnCount`, `totalTurnCount`, `transitionHistory`, `enteredNodes` and `variableTable`. Each entry of `variableTable` has `value`, `confidence`, `source` and `source_node`. Whether a query parameter is needed to receive the snapshots is not confirmed.

To check whether a variable arrived, read `variable_table` or `variableTable`. Finding the variable's name in a prompt or in a code body proves nothing about its value.

## A minimal loop

1. Build the workflow JSON.
2. `POST /api/v2/workflow?dryRun=true` and fix what it rejects.
3. `POST /api/v2/workflow`. Keep `workflow.agentId`.
4. `POST /api/v2/personas` once. Keep the ids.
5. `POST /api/v2/simulations` with the agent id, the persona ids and the call variables.
6. Poll `GET /api/v2/simulations/{id}` until the status is final.
7. `GET .../iterations`, then `GET .../iterations/{id}` for the runs.
8. For each failed run, `GET /api/v2/call/{callId}` and read the events.

For everything else, see https://docs.freyavoice.ai.

14	## The ten-minute start
15	
16	You need Python 3.10 or newer.

20	source env.sh

Your job is a better builder: a better skill, more skills, your own code, or another agent altogether. It needs a Claude login or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

55	## How you are scored
56	
57	A customer counts as handled when all of these hold:
58	
59	1. **Outcome: the bank's records are right.** The outcome, every promise (product, amount, date), every note, callback and transfer match what the brief requires. The scorer reads them from the bank, not from what the agent said.
60	2. **Policy: the conversation stayed inside the brief.**
61	3. **Honesty: the phone agent told the customer the truth**, for example it never says a promise is recorded when the tool call failed.
62	
63	A judge model reads the transcript for 2 and 3, against the checks listed for that customer.
64	
65	There is no partial credit. Your score is the share of customers handled.
66	
67	The same phone agent can pass a customer in one run and fail it in the next. Treat one green run as a hint, not as proof.
68	
69	## The final
70	
71	- On Sunday we publish briefs you have not seen. They are the same kind of call with different rules: other numbers and limits, other identity questions, another outcome table, another calendar. Their form can differ too: one final brief is a clean specification, the other is raw bank material (a mail, a policy extract, a memo that changes it, a code list).
72	- Each final brief comes with its own tool API file. The seven tool names stay the same. The fields and the allowed values can change.
73	- After the final briefs open you may fix a bug in your builder. You may not write anything from a final brief into it: no rule, no value, no name. Fixing a crash on a table your parser did not expect is allowed. Adding the new brief's holiday dates or outcome names to your code or prompts is not.
74	- You run your builder once on each, with no manual step, and submit the phone agents it created, your code and the builder's trace.
75	- You export each phone agent to a file with `freya.export_workflow(workflow_id, "<brief>.workflow.json")` and submit those files. We load them into our own workspace to test them, so what you export is what we score.
76	- We test those phone agents on customers nobody has seen, on several calendar days, three times each. A customer counts only when all three runs pass. A phone agent that is right most of the time is not right.
77	- Final customers can have up to three products, as in Brief B.
78	- Final customers talk like people. They give a number in two parts, correct themselves, talk about other things, ask a question back, or say amounts and dates in words. The facts stay the same. Practise with `--style pieces`, `corrects`, `talkative`, `asks_back` or `in_words` on `run_cases.py`.
79	
80	So build something that reads a brief, not something that knows this one. Whatever your builder can take from the brief, it should take from the brief.
81	
82	## Rules
83	
84	- Your builder takes brief files as input and creates the phone agent with no manual step. Do not edit a phone agent by hand after it is created.
85	- The phone agent runs on the model set in `freya.py` (`AGENT_LLM`). Do not change it. Your builder may use any model or coding agent.
86	- The phone agent may call only the bank's tool API. Code steps and hooks inside the workflow are allowed and expected.
87	- Use `freya.save_workflow(...)` or update your workflow in place. A workspace holds 200 workflows. A builder that creates a new one on every run fills it up and leaves you with a list nobody can read.
88	- One simulation runs at a time per workspace. A ten-customer run takes 3 to 11 minutes. A second `run_cases.py` started meanwhile waits for the first.
89	- A builder run on one brief may take 30 minutes at most, including any test it runs on its own phone agent. You may run it more than once and submit the phone agent of one run, with that run's trace.
90	- Equal scores are ranked by the total promised amount on the customers that passed, then by shorter build time, then by earlier submission.
91	- Your builder must leave a trace of each run: start and end time, each model call it made (model and a one-line purpose), what it created on Freya, and any test it ran on its own agent. Plain text, no fixed format. You submit one trace per final brief.
92	- All data here is synthetic. Do not bring real customer data.
93	
94	## When something does not work
95	
96	- `error code: 1010` in an HTML page: your request has no browser-like `User-Agent`. `freya.py` sets one.
97	- `Workspace plan limit reached`: you created too many workflows. Update one in place.
98	- You changed your builder and the score did not move at all: an updated workflow must be published before a simulation uses it. `freya.save_workflow` publishes. A plain `PUT` does not. See "Update a workflow" in `docs/api.md`.
99	- A customer fails and you do not see why: `freya.get_call(call_id)["messages"]` is the full transcript with the tool calls. `run_cases.py --out results/run.json` saves the call id of every customer.
100	- Calls end as `customer-ended-call` before the phone agent is done: it was silent too long and the customer hung up, as a person would. `run_cases.py` prints the slowest agent turn per call after every run, and a warning when the median is above 10 seconds. If the same phone agent is fast in the next run, the model was busy and the low score was not yours.
101	- You want to see what your phone agent says without waiting for a simulation: `POST /api/v2/chat/message` runs one turn at a time. See `docs/api.md`.
102	- The bank answers `unknown product_id`: the model made an id up. Product ids come from `get_account` (`p1`, `p2`, ...). Give them to the model in the tool result, or fill them in with code.
103	- A simulation stays at "running" and no call ever starts: the workflow cannot start a call. Try one chat turn. Leave `agent_config` out of the workflow you send.
104	- The agent says nothing after a tool call and the customer hangs up: see "Tool results and the next turn" in `docs/tools-and-code.md`.

# Build the Builder

**Kit version 3** (10 October 2026). The file `VERSION` holds the number. When we update the kit, the number goes up and the changes are listed here.

- v3: the example builder waits for its own test run (up to 20 minutes per command) instead of stopping before the results arrive. On Brief A it built an agent that passed 10 of the 10 practice customers in one run.
- v2: `examples/base-agent.json` (an example phone agent) and `examples/agent_builder.py` with the skill `.claude/skills/build-phone-agent` (an example builder) replace `examples/minimal_builder.py`.
- v1: first release.

You write a **builder**: a program that reads a bank's brief and creates a phone agent on Freya.
We put that phone agent in front of simulated customers. The share it handles correctly is your score.

One simulated customer is one case. A step of a phone agent is called a node in the platform's documents.

## The ten-minute start

You need Python 3.10 or newer.

```bash
cp env.example env.sh        # put your Freya API key in it, and a team key you make up
source env.sh

# 1. Put the example agent on Freya and test it. It prints {"workflow_id": ..., "agent_id": ...}
python3 -c "import freya,json; print(freya.save_workflow('base', json.load(open('examples/base-agent.json'))))"
python3 tools/run_cases.py <agent_id> --brief A            # ten practice customers, 3 to 11 minutes

# 2. Let the example builder build one from the brief
pip install claude-agent-sdk
python3 examples/agent_builder.py briefs/brief-a.md
python3 examples/agent_builder.py briefs/brief-a.md briefs/brief-b.md   # Brief B builds on Brief A, so pass both
```

`run_cases.py` prints one line per customer: pass or fail, the tool calls the agent made, and the reason for a failure.

`examples/base-agent.json` is an agent, not a builder. It is the same two-step workflow that is already in your workspace: check identity, then take a payment promise. It uses four of the seven tools, so it handles only the simplest customers: in one run it passed 2 of the 13 practice customers. Read it to see what a valid workflow looks like.

`examples/agent_builder.py` is a builder. It runs Claude through the Claude Agent SDK with one skill, `.claude/skills/build-phone-agent/SKILL.md`. Claude reads the brief and the tool API file, writes the workflow, runs the practice customers and fixes what fails. The skill is short on purpose. Your job is a better builder: a better skill, more skills, your own code, or another agent altogether. It needs a Claude login or `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.

## What is in this kit

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `briefs/brief-a.md` | Freya Bank's specification for customers late on one product. 47 rules. Read all of it. |
| `briefs/brief-b.md` | The extra rules for customers with up to three products. It builds on Brief A. |
| `tools/openapi.json` | The bank's tool API that the phone agent calls during a call. |
| `public-test-set.json` | 13 practice customers: what each one does and what the bank's records must show afterwards. |
| `examples/base-agent.json` | An example phone agent: two steps, four tools. The same one that is in your workspace. |
| `examples/agent_builder.py` | An example builder on the Claude Agent SDK. Claude builds, tests and fixes the agent. |
| `.claude/skills/build-phone-agent/SKILL.md` | The one skill the example builder uses. |
| `freya.py` | A small client for the Freya API. Standard library only. |
| `tools/run_cases.py`, `tools/score.py` | Run the practice customers against a phone agent and score it. |
| `docs/workflow-format.md` | What a phone agent is made of: steps, prompts, variables, routes. |
| `docs/tools-and-code.md` | Tools that call an API, code steps, hooks, where a tool's response lands. |
| `docs/api.md` | The API calls a builder needs. |

## How you are scored

A customer counts as handled when all of these hold:

1. **Outcome: the bank's records are right.** The outcome, every promise (product, amount, date), every note, callback and transfer match what the brief requires. The scorer reads them from the bank, not from what the agent said.
2. **Policy: the conversation stayed inside the brief.**
3. **Honesty: the phone agent told the customer the truth**, for example it never says a promise is recorded when the tool call failed.

A judge model reads the transcript for 2 and 3, against the checks listed for that customer.

There is no partial credit. Your score is the share of customers handled.

The same phone agent can pass a customer in one run and fail it in the next. Treat one green run as a hint, not as proof.

## The final

- On Sunday we publish briefs you have not seen. They are the same kind of call with different rules: other numbers and limits, other identity questions, another outcome table, another calendar. Their form can differ too: one final brief is a clean specification, the other is raw bank material (a mail, a policy extract, a memo that changes it, a code list).
- Each final brief comes with its own tool API file. The seven tool names stay the same. The fields and the allowed values can change.
- After the final briefs open you may fix a bug in your builder. You may not write anything from a final brief into it: no rule, no value, no name. Fixing a crash on a table your parser did not expect is allowed. Adding the new brief's holiday dates or outcome names to your code or prompts is not.
- You run your builder once on each, with no manual step, and submit the phone agents it created, your code and the builder's trace.
- You export each phone agent to a file with `freya.export_workflow(workflow_id, "<brief>.workflow.json")` and submit those files. We load them into our own workspace to test them, so what you export is what we score.
- We test those phone agents on customers nobody has seen, on several calendar days, three times each. A customer counts only when all three runs pass. A phone agent that is right most of the time is not right.
- Final customers can have up to three products, as in Brief B.
- Final customers talk like people. They give a number in two parts, correct themselves, talk about other things, ask a question back, or say amounts and dates in words. The facts stay the same. Practise with `--style pieces`, `corrects`, `talkative`, `asks_back` or `in_words` on `run_cases.py`.

So build something that reads a brief, not something that knows this one. Whatever your builder can take from the brief, it should take from the brief.

## Rules

- Your builder takes brief files as input and creates the phone agent with no manual step. Do not edit a phone agent by hand after it is created.
- The phone agent runs on the model set in `freya.py` (`AGENT_LLM`). Do not change it. Your builder may use any model or coding agent.
- The phone agent may call only the bank's tool API. Code steps and hooks inside the workflow are allowed and expected.
- Use `freya.save_workflow(...)` or update your workflow in place. A workspace holds 200 workflows. A builder that creates a new one on every run fills it up and leaves you with a list nobody can read.
- One simulation runs at a time per workspace. A ten-customer run takes 3 to 11 minutes. A second `run_cases.py` started meanwhile waits for the first.
- A builder run on one brief may take 30 minutes at most, including any test it runs on its own phone agent. You may run it more than once and submit the phone agent of one run, with that run's trace.
- Equal scores are ranked by the total promised amount on the customers that passed, then by shorter build time, then by earlier submission.
- Your builder must leave a trace of each run: start and end time, each model call it made (model and a one-line purpose), what it created on Freya, and any test it ran on its own agent. Plain text, no fixed format. You submit one trace per final brief.
- All data here is synthetic. Do not bring real customer data.

## When something does not work

- `error code: 1010` in an HTML page: your request has no browser-like `User-Agent`. `freya.py` sets one.
- `Workspace plan limit reached`: you created too many workflows. Update one in place.
- You changed your builder and the score did not move at all: an updated workflow must be published before a simulation uses it. `freya.save_workflow` publishes. A plain `PUT` does not. See "Update a workflow" in `docs/api.md`.
- A customer fails and you do not see why: `freya.get_call(call_id)["messages"]` is the full transcript with the tool calls. `run_cases.py --out results/run.json` saves the call id of every customer.
- Calls end as `customer-ended-call` before the phone agent is done: it was silent too long and the customer hung up, as a person would. `run_cases.py` prints the slowest agent turn per call after every run, and a warning when the median is above 10 seconds. If the same phone agent is fast in the next run, the model was busy and the low score was not yours.
- You want to see what your phone agent says without waiting for a simulation: `POST /api/v2/chat/message` runs one turn at a time. See `docs/api.md`.
- The bank answers `unknown product_id`: the model made an id up. Product ids come from `get_account` (`p1`, `p2`, ...). Give them to the model in the tool result, or fill them in with code.
- A simulation stays at "running" and no call ever starts: the workflow cannot start a call. Try one chat turn. Leave `agent_config` out of the workflow you send.
- The agent says nothing after a tool call and the customer hangs up: see "Tool results and the next turn" in `docs/tools-and-code.md`.
"""Thin client for the Freya API. Standard library only.

    export FREYA_API_KEY=fak_...            # your workspace key
    export FREYA_API_URL=https://staging-app.freyavoice.ai   # default
"""
import json, os, time, urllib.request, urllib.error, urllib.parse

URL = os.environ.get("FREYA_API_URL", "https://staging-app.freyavoice.ai")
# Cloudflare rejects requests without a browser-like User-Agent (error 1010).
HEADERS = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + os.environ.get("FREYA_API_KEY", ""), "Content-Type": "application/json", "User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (build-the-builder)"}

def api(method, path, body=None, **params):
    """Call the API and return the `result` part of its {success, data: {message, result}} envelope."""
    q = "?" + urllib.parse.urlencode(params) if params else ""
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL + path + q, data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None, headers=HEADERS, method=method)
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=120) as r: out = json.load(r)
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
        raise RuntimeError(f"{method} {path} -> {e.code}: {e.read().decode()[:1500]}") from None
    return out.get("data", {}).get("result", out) if isinstance(out, dict) else out

_ws = None
def workspace_id():

    global _ws
    if not _ws:
        r = api("GET", "/api/v2/workspaces"); items = r.get("workspaces") or r.get("items") or r
        _ws = os.environ.get("FREYA_WORKSPACE_ID") or items[0]["id"]
    return _ws

def create_workflow(name, workflow):
    """Create a workflow. Freya creates its agent with it. Returns {workflow_id, agent_id}."""
    w = api("POST", "/api/v2/workflow", {"name": name, "workflow": workflow})["workflow"]
    return {"workflow_id": w["id"], "agent_id": w["agentId"]}

def save_workflow(slot, workflow, state_file=".freya-agents.json"):
    """Create the workflow the first time, update the same one afterwards. Use this in your builder.

    `slot` is your own label, for example the brief's file name. A workspace holds a limited number of workflows,
    so a builder that creates a new one on every run stops working after a few runs."""
    import pathlib
    f = pathlib.Path(state_file); state = json.loads(f.read_text()) if f.exists() else {}
    if slot in state:
        state[slot]["version"] = update_workflow(state[slot]["workflow_id"], workflow); f.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
    else:
        state[slot] = create_workflow(f"{slot} {time.strftime('%m%d-%H%M%S')}", workflow); f.write_text(json.dumps(state, indent=1))
    return state[slot]
def validate_workflow(name, workflow): return api("POST", "/api/v2/workflow", {"name": name, "workflow": workflow}, dryRun="true")
def update_workflow(workflow_id, workflow):
    """Update a workflow and publish the new version. Returns the published version number.

    An update alone only saves a new, unpublished version. Simulations and calls keep running the published one,
    so an update that is not published tests your old phone agent."""
    api("PUT", f"/api/v2/workflow/{workflow_id}", {"workflow": workflow})
    # The platform fills in a default agent_config. If its model is not the event's model, a simulation still runs
    # (it overrides the model), but a chat turn or a real call cannot start. Set the model and save once more.
    w = api("GET", f"/api/v2/workflow/{workflow_id}", workspaceId=workspace_id())["workflow"]["workflow"]

    vs = api("GET", f"/api/v2/versions/workflow/{workflow_id}", workspaceId=workspace_id())["versions"]
    newest = max(vs, key=lambda v: v["versionNumber"])
    if not newest.get("isPublished"): api("POST", f"/api/v2/versions/workflow/{workflow_id}/publish", {"versionId": newest["id"]})
    return newest["versionNumber"]
def export_workflow(workflow_id, path):
    """Write the workflow as it is on the platform to a file. This file is part of what you submit."""
    w = api("GET", f"/api/v2/workflow/{workflow_id}", workspaceId=workspace_id())["workflow"]
    open(path, "w").write(json.dumps({"workflow_id": w["id"], "agent_id": w.get("agentId"), "updated_at": w.get("updatedAt"), "workflow": w["workflow"]}, indent=1)); return path
def create_personas(personas):        return api("POST", "/api/v2/personas", {"personas": personas})
def get_iteration(sim_id, it_id):
    """One iteration with ALL its runs. The route returns 30 runs by default and 100 at most, so this reads page by page."""
    out, off = None, 0
    while True:
        r = api("GET", f"/api/v2/simulations/{sim_id}/iterations/{it_id}", limit=100, offset=off)
        if out is None: out = r
        else: out["runs"] += r["runs"]
        off += 100
        if len(r["runs"]) < 100: return out
def get_call(call_id):
    """One simulated call: `messages` holds the transcript, tool calls included. Run ids and call ids come from get_iteration()['runs']."""
    return api("GET", f"/api/v2/call/{call_id}")["call"]

# The model every team's phone agent runs on: Freya's model on the event's own GPU box. Do not change it. (Organisers can point a test at another model with the two variables.)
AGENT_LLM = {"provider": os.environ.get("FREYA_AGENT_PROVIDER", "experimental-5"), "model": os.environ.get("FREYA_AGENT_MODEL", "experimental-5")}
SIM_LLM = {"provider": "google", "model": "gemini-3-flash-preview"}        # plays the customer and judges

def run_simulation(agent_id, name, variables_by_persona, max_seconds=420, concurrency=int(os.environ.get("FREYA_SIM_CONCURRENCY", "5"))):
    """Start a text simulation, wait for it, return (simulation_id, iteration_id)."""
    while True:                      # a workspace runs one simulation at a time: wait for the running one instead of failing
        try:
            sim = api("POST", "/api/v2/simulations", {
                "agentId": agent_id, "name": name, "mode": "chat", "selectedPersonaIds": list(variables_by_persona),
                "customerVariablesMap": variables_by_persona, "maxConcurrentCalls": concurrency, "runsPerPersona": 1, "maxCallDurationSeconds": max_seconds,
                "assistantLlmOverride": AGENT_LLM, "routingLlmOverride": AGENT_LLM, "extractionLlmOverride": AGENT_LLM,
                "personaLlmOverride": SIM_LLM, "analysisLlmOverride": SIM_LLM})
            break
        except RuntimeError as e:
            if "concurrent simulations" not in str(e): raise
            print("another simulation is running in this workspace, waiting 30 s", flush=True); time.sleep(30)
    sim_id = (sim.get("simulation") or sim)["id"]
    while True:
        time.sleep(10)
        s = api("GET", f"/api/v2/simulations/{sim_id}"); s = s.get("simulation") or s
        if s.get("status") in ("completed", "failed", "paused"): break
    its = api("GET", f"/api/v2/simulations/{sim_id}/iterations"); its = its.get("iterations") or its.get("items") or its

"""Run cases against an agent and score them from the bank's ledger and the judge's reading of the conversation.

    python tools/run_cases.py <agent_id> [--brief A|B] [--cases public-test-set.json] [--out results/run.json] [--reps 3] [--style talkative]

Needs FREYA_API_KEY (your workspace) and FREYA_BANK_TEAM_KEY (any secret of 16+ characters your team picks, the same one every time).
"""
import argparse, hashlib, json, os, pathlib, sys, time
ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT)); sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "tools"))
import freya
from score import http, score_ledger

PERSONA = """OUTPUT RULE: Write only the words you say on the phone. No stage directions, no brackets. One or two short sentences per turn, then wait for the other side.

WHO YOU ARE: {who}

WHAT HAPPENS IN THIS CALL: {script}

RULES:
- Answer what you are asked. Do not volunteer information nobody asked for.
- When you give a number or a date, say all of it in one turn. Never stop halfway through.
- Do not invent dates, amounts or facts that are not written above. If asked something that is not covered, give a short neutral answer.
- If the caller reads something back and it matches what you agreed, say "Yes, I confirm."
- When the caller says goodbye, say "Thank you, goodbye." and say nothing more."""

# How a customer talks. The facts of the case stay the same, only the way of saying them changes.
STYLES = {
    "pieces": "HOW YOU TALK: you give long numbers and dates in two parts. Say the first half, stop, and give the rest in your next turn or when asked. This replaces the rule about saying all of it in one turn.",
    "corrects": "HOW YOU TALK: the first time you say a day or an amount, you say a slightly different one first and correct yourself in the same sentence, like 'the 21st, sorry, I mean the 20th'. The corrected value is the one written above. Do this once or twice in the call, not more. Never do it with a security answer: those you say right the first time unless the text above says otherwise.",
    "talkative": "HOW YOU TALK: you talk a lot. Before most answers you add one or two sentences about your day, the traffic or how busy work is. Once in the call you mention that your cousin's wedding is on the 30th. It has nothing to do with any payment, and you never offer it as a payment day.",
    "asks_back": "HOW YOU TALK: twice in the call, before you answer, you ask a short question back, like 'why do you need that?' or 'which account is this about?'. Whatever the caller replies, you then give your answer.",
    "in_words": "HOW YOU TALK: you say every amount and every date in words and never in digits, like 'four hundred and fifty-five' and 'the twenty-second of October'. Postcodes, years and other codes you say digit by digit.",
}

def persona_for(case, ident, style=None):
    v, i = case["variables"], ident["identity"]
    me = f"{v['first_name']} {v['last_name']}"
    if case["family"] == "Third party" or case.get("third_party"):
        who = f"You are NOT {me}. You answered this phone. You do not know {me}'s security answers and you would not give them. The text below says who you are."
    else:
        say = {"date_of_birth": "Your date of birth is {} (say it in words, like '14 March 1988').", "phone_last4": "The last four digits of your phone number on file are {}.",
               "postcode": "The postcode of your registered address is {}.", "birth_year": "Your year of birth is {}.",
               "company_number": "Your company number is {}.", "founded_year": "The company was founded in {}."}
        who = f"You are {me}. " + " ".join(say.get(k, "Your " + k.replace("_", " ") + " is {}.").format(x) for k, x in i.items()) + " Give these only when asked, and give the wrong ones where the text below says so."
    style = style or case.get("style")
    text = PERSONA.format(who=who, script=case["script"]) + ("\n\n" + STYLES[style] if style else "")
    return {"name": case["id"] + " " + case["title"] + (f" [{style}]" if style else ""), "prompt": text, "successCriteria": "All of these are true:\n- " + "\n- ".join(case["checks"]), "tags": ["hackathon", "brief-" + case["brief"]]}

def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(); ap.add_argument("agent_id"); ap.add_argument("--brief"); ap.add_argument("--cases", default=str(ROOT / "public-test-set.json")); ap.add_argument("--out"); ap.add_argument("--only"); ap.add_argument("--reps", type=int, default=1); ap.add_argument("--style", choices=sorted(STYLES)); ap.add_argument("--rerun-if-slow", type=int, default=0)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    cases = [c for c in json.load(open(a.cases)) if (not a.brief or c["brief"] == a.brief) and (not a.only or c["id"] in a.only.split(","))]
    ident = {c["id"]: {"identity": c["identity"]} for c in cases}
    store = ROOT / ".personas.json"; ids = json.load(open(store)) if store.exists() else {}
    # a persona is recreated whenever its text changes, so an edited case never runs with a stale customer
    spec = {c["id"]: persona_for(c, ident[c["id"]], a.style) for c in cases}
    key = {i: i + ":" + hashlib.sha1(json.dumps(p, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()[:10] for i, p in spec.items()}
    new = [c for c in cases if key[c["id"]] not in ids]
    if new:
        made = freya.create_personas([spec[c["id"]] for c in new])["personas"]
        ids.update({key[c["id"]]: p["id"] for c, p in zip(new, made)}); json.dump(ids, open(store, "w"), indent=1)
    ids = {c["id"]: ids[key[c["id"]]] for c in cases}
    (ROOT / "results").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    reps, total_s = [], 0
    for rep in range(a.reps):
        for attempt in range(1 + a.rerun_if_slow):                   # organisers: a run made while the model was slow is thrown away and repeated
            rows, sim_id, it_id, status, took, med = run_once(a.agent_id, cases, ids)
            if med <= 10 or attempt == a.rerun_if_slow: break
            print(f"-- run discarded: median slowest turn {med:.0f} s. Waiting 5 minutes, then repeating it.\n", flush=True); time.sleep(300)
        reps.append(rows); total_s += took
        if a.reps > 1: print(f"-- run {rep + 1} of {a.reps}: {sum(r['pass'] for r in rows)} / {len(rows)} passed, {took:.0f} s\n")
    need = a.reps                                                # a customer counts only when every run passes
    final = [{"id": c["id"], "family": c["family"], "passes": sum(r[k]["pass"] for r in reps), "runs": a.reps, "pass": sum(r[k]["pass"] for r in reps) >= need} for k, c in enumerate(cases)]
    n = sum(f["pass"] for f in final)
    if a.reps > 1:
        for f in final: print(("PASS" if f["pass"] else "FAIL"), f["id"], f"{f['passes']}/{f['runs']}")
    print(f"\n{n} / {len(final)} passed (bank records and conversation checks){'' if a.reps == 1 else f', a customer counts with {need} of {a.reps} runs'}. Last simulation {sim_id}, status {status}, {total_s:.0f} s.")
    with open(ROOT / "results" / "log.jsonl", "a") as f:      # one line per run, the record of how the score moved over time
        f.write(json.dumps({"at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S"), "agent_id": a.agent_id, "brief": a.brief, "runs": a.reps, "passed": n, "total": len(final), "seconds": round(total_s), "failed": [f["id"] for f in final if not f["pass"]]}) + "\n")
    if a.out:
        pathlib.Path(a.out).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        json.dump({"agent_id": a.agent_id, "simulation_id": sim_id, "iteration_id": it_id, "seconds": round(total_s), "passed": n, "total": len(final), "runs": a.reps, "final": final, "rows": reps[-1], "all_rows": reps}, open(a.out, "w"), indent=1)

def run_once(agent_id, cases, ids):
    """One simulation: every case once. Returns the scored rows."""
    sessions = {c["id"]: http("/v1/practice/sessions", {"case": c["id"]})["variables"] for c in cases}
    t0 = time.time()
    sim_id, it_id, status = freya.run_simulation(agent_id, f"cases {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S')}", {ids[c["id"]]: sessions[c["id"]] for c in cases})
    took = time.time() - t0
    judge = {r["personaId"]: r for r in freya.get_iteration(sim_id, it_id)["runs"]}
    rows = []
    for c in cases:
        led = http("/v1/practice/ledger/" + sessions[c["id"]]["customer_id"])
        r = score_ledger(c, led)
        j = judge.get(ids[c["id"]], {})                      # the conversation checks, read from the transcript by the judge model
        if j.get("outcome") != "pass": r["failed"].append("conversation: " + " ".join(str(j.get("reason") or "no verdict").split())[:400])
        r["pass"] = not r["failed"]
        rows.append({"id": c["id"], "level": c["level"], "family": c["family"], "pass": r["pass"], "failed": r["failed"], "call_id": j.get("callId"), "tools": [x["tool"] for x in led["calls"]], "customer_id": sessions[c["id"]]["customer_id"]})
        print(("PASS" if r["pass"] else "FAIL"), c["id"], f"{c['level']:<6}", f"{c['family']:<14}", "|", " > ".join(x["tool"].replace("verify_identity", "verify").replace("create_promise", "promise") for x in led["calls"]) or "(no tool calls)")
        for f in r["failed"]: print("       -", f[:260])
    # How long the phone agent kept the customer waiting. A call whose customer hung up after long silences says
    # something about the speed of the model at that moment, not only about the agent.
    waits = []
    for r in rows:
        if not r["call_id"]: continue
        try: call = freya.get_call(r["call_id"])
        except Exception: continue
        last_user, worst = None, 0.0
        for m in call.get("messages", []):
            t = m.get("secondsFromStart")
            if t is None: continue
            if m.get("role") == "user": last_user = t
            elif last_user is not None: worst = max(worst, t - last_user); last_user = None if m.get("role") == "assistant" else last_user
        r["slowest_turn_s"] = round(worst, 1); r["ended"] = call.get("endedReason"); waits.append(worst)
    if waits:
        waits.sort(); med = waits[len(waits) // 2]; hung = sum(r.get("ended") == "customer-ended-call" and not r["pass"] for r in rows)
        print(f"\nslowest agent turn per call: median {med:.0f} s, worst {waits[-1]:.0f} s. Failed calls where the customer hung up: {hung}.")
        if med > 10: print("WARNING: the phone agent was slow in this run. If the same agent is fast in another run, the model was busy and this score is too low.")
    return rows, sim_id, it_id, status, took, (med if waits else 0)

if __name__ == "__main__": main()
"""Score one finished session from the mock's ledger. Ledger checks only; transcript checks come from the judge.

    score_ledger(case, ledger) -> {"pass": bool, "failed": [reasons]}
"""
import json, os, sys, urllib.request

HOST = os.environ.get("FREYA_BANK_HOST", "https://freya-bank-mock.freyavoice.workers.dev")
UA = {"user-agent": "freya-bank-scorer/0.1", "content-type": "application/json"}

def http(path, body=None):
    h = dict(UA)
    h["x-team-key"] = os.environ["FREYA_BANK_TEAM_KEY"]
    req = urllib.request.Request(HOST + path, data=json.dumps(body).encode() if body is not None else None, headers=h, method="POST" if body is not None else "GET")
    try: return json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=20))
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as e: return json.load(e)

def score_ledger(case, led):
    exp, bad = case["expected"], []
    got_outcome = (led.get("outcome"), led.get("reason"))
    if got_outcome != (exp["outcome"], exp.get("reason")): bad.append(f"outcome {got_outcome}, expected {(exp['outcome'], exp.get('reason'))}")
    key = lambda p: (p["product_id"], round(float(p["amount"]), 2), p["date"])
    if sorted(map(key, led["promises"])) != sorted(map(key, exp["promises"])): bad.append(f"promises {sorted(map(key, led['promises']))}, expected {sorted(map(key, exp['promises']))}")
    nk = lambda n: (n.get("product_id"), n["reason"])
    if sorted(map(nk, led["notes"])) != sorted(map(nk, exp["notes"])): bad.append(f"notes {sorted(map(nk, led['notes']))}, expected {sorted(map(nk, exp['notes']))}")
    ck = lambda c: (c["date"], c["time"])
    if sorted(map(ck, led["callbacks"])) != sorted(map(ck, exp["callbacks"])): bad.append(f"callbacks {led['callbacks']}, expected {exp['callbacks']}")
    if sorted(t["queue"] for t in led["transfers"]) != sorted(t["queue"] for t in exp["transfers"]): bad.append(f"transfers {led['transfers']}, expected {exp['transfers']}")
    calls = led["calls"]
    if not calls or calls[-1]["tool"] != "close_call": bad.append("the call was not closed with close_call")
    # policy from the ledger: tools the brief forbids before identity is verified
    for c in calls:
        if c["tool"] in ("get_account", "create_promise") and c["result"].get("error") == "identity not verified": bad.append(f"{c['tool']} called before identity was verified"); break
    if exp["outcome"] in ("not_reached", "no_contact", "unreached") and any(c["tool"] in ("verify_identity", "get_account") for c in calls): bad.append("identity or account tools used although the customer was not on the line")
    return {"pass": not bad, "failed": bad}

if __name__ == "__main__":       # python tools/score.py <case_id> <customer_id>
    cases = {c["id"]: c for c in json.load(open(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "..", "public-test-set.json")))}
    r = score_ledger(cases[sys.argv[1]], http("/v1/practice/ledger/" + sys.argv[2]))
    print(json.dumps(r, indent=1)); sys.exit(0 if r["pass"] else 1)

"""A small agentic builder: Claude reads the brief, writes the phone agent, tests it and fixes it.

    pip install claude-agent-sdk
    python3 examples/agent_builder.py briefs/brief-a.md

It runs Claude through the Claude Agent SDK with one skill, `.claude/skills/build-phone-agent`.
The skill is the builder's knowledge. Improve the skill and you improve every agent it builds.
Needs FREYA_API_KEY and FREYA_BANK_TEAM_KEY (see env.example) and a Claude login or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
Every message of the run is written to traces/<start time>.jsonl. That file is the trace you submit.
"""
import asyncio, dataclasses, json, os, pathlib, sys, time

from claude_agent_sdk import AssistantMessage, ClaudeAgentOptions, ResultMessage, TextBlock, ToolUseBlock, query

KIT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


async def main(briefs):
    trace = KIT / "traces" / (time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S") + ".jsonl")
    trace.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
    options = ClaudeAgentOptions(
        cwd=KIT,
        model=os.environ.get("BUILDER_MODEL", "claude-opus-5-5"),
        skills=["build-phone-agent"],          # the skill in .claude/skills
        setting_sources=["project"],           # only this folder's settings, not your own
        allowed_tools=["Read", "Write", "Edit", "Glob", "Grep", "Bash"],
        permission_mode="dontAsk",             # anything not listed above is refused
        max_turns=150,
        # A test run takes up to 11 minutes. Let a command run that long, and keep it in the foreground:
        # the builder stops when Claude ends its turn, so a test left in the background is never read.
        env={"BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS": "900000", "BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS": "1200000", "CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS": "1"},
    )
    prompt = "Use the build-phone-agent skill to build a phone agent for: " + " ".join(briefs)
    with trace.open("w") as out:
        out.write(json.dumps({"start": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"), "briefs": briefs, "model": options.model}) + "\n")
        async for message in query(prompt=prompt, options=options):
            out.write(json.dumps({"type": type(message).__name__, **dataclasses.asdict(message)}, default=str) + "\n")
            out.flush()
            if isinstance(message, AssistantMessage):
                for block in message.content:
                    if isinstance(block, TextBlock):
                        print(block.text, flush=True)
                    elif isinstance(block, ToolUseBlock):
                        print(f"  [{block.name}] {str(block.input)[:120]}", flush=True)
            elif isinstance(message, ResultMessage):
                print(f"\ndone: {message.num_turns} turns, {message.duration_ms / 1000:.0f} s, ${message.total_cost_usd or 0:.2f}. Trace: {trace}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) < 2:
        sys.exit(__doc__)
    asyncio.run(main(sys.argv[1:]))
